label: mid/late original-phase steps (t=4-6) after a z, or right after v
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 99% of activation mass is there, the delimiter step holds about 1%, and it never fires in the copy phase. It is limited to positions t=3-7, with 97% of mass at t=4-6 and the peak at t=5. It does not depend on L, apart from being rare for L<=5. Within that window it depends on the prefix. The strongest activations follow a z earlier in the sequence (top examples look like x z z ... v then the next token), or come at the step right after a v input (prev_tok=v, 6x lift). The prefix rule "t in 4-6 and (z seen earlier or previous input is v)" captures 82% of activation mass but only 65% of active steps, at 37% precision. Weaker activations come from other prefix combinations (prev s/c/j/i, prev2 l/s) that do not reduce to a simple rule. Larger activations are linked to a z seen earlier: the seen-z rule covers 80% of the top activation quartile but only 30% of the bottom quartile. It does not depend on the identity of the current input token, digit count or repeats.
